static_traits.name: Lin Ruosi
static_traits.educational_background: High school graduate (valedictorian), later dropped out of college to care for grandparents
static_traits.family_status: Father is an insurance salesman, Mother full-time caring for her and siblings; after dropping out of college, long-term help caring for grandparents
static_traits.social_status: Has supportive family and friends, but due to Inferiority and low self-worth, relationships are somewhat strained, both pushing others away and excessively seeking comfort from others; not easily opening up about feelings of inferiority
static_traits.medical_history: No obvious physical illness; no psychotherapy received in the past; no similar psychological problems before
static_traits.language_features: Steady speech rate and tone, organized narration, with self-Reflection ability; tending to use Self-deprecation and uncertain expressions (like 'I feel''maybe'); high cooperation, willing to try journaling and restructuring thoughts

basic_info.main_problem: Because I dropped out of university that year to care for my grandparents, I overall feel very 'stupid', triggering long-term inferiority and low self-worth, especially more obvious in tasks requiring critical thinking or problem-solving.
basic_info.core_demands: Persistent inferiority and low self-worth have affected daily life and emotional health, hence seeking counseling; hoping to identify and question negative thoughts, practicing replacing them with more balanced, realistic thoughts, thereby improving self-esteem and confidence.
growth_experiences: During High school, academic performance was outstanding (valedictorian). After entering college, chose to drop out because grandparents needed care. This decision triggered long-term self-criticism and regret, strongly tying one's ability and worth to educational credentials, believing academic and career opportunities were missed, and more easily activating inferiority and low self-worth when facing thinking-type tasks. In the family of origin, Father is an insurance salesman, Mother is a Full-time homemaker, raising her and her siblings; after dropping out, long-term help caring for grandparents.

core_beliefs: My worth depends on whether I complete higher education
I will most likely fail at important tasks

special_situations.event: When facing tasks requiring critical thinking or problem solving (such as financial planning, important decisions)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot get things right immediately and think through problems like degree holders, it proves I am stupid and have no value
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding or procrastinating on tasks, first seeking comfort and guidance from others, minimizing independent decision-making
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I definitely cannot do well; I am just stupid

special_situations.event: Comparing with more highly educated people, or thinking about not yet finishing one's studies
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not have a College degree, I am worse than others and doomed to be inferior
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Self-deprecates to lower others' expectations, avoids comparison settings or contact with others
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They have degrees so they must be stronger than me; I am not as good as them

special_situations.event: Repeatedly recalling the 'if I had not dropped out' scenario and comparing with oneself
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Since I made that choice, all current setbacks are caused by it; current efforts and strengths do not count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Indulging in ruminating on the past, ignoring existing contributions and achievements
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I missed the key opportunity of life; everything bad now is because I dropped out

special_situations.event: When interacting with others requires displaying ability (such as helping a friend with financial planning or speaking in a group discussion)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Others' approval determines my value; if they do not affirm me, it means I am worthless
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Excessively seeking reassurance and affirmation from others, or distancing from/avoiding the relationship afterward to reduce chances of being evaluated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will think I am stupid; if I perform poorly I will be looked down upon

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized as capable and worthy of acceptance, with one's value seen even without completing higher education
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being judged as stupid or incompetent, Being rejected or humiliated; worrying that personal choices cause irreversible losses
defense_goal: Preemptively reducing external negation through self-criticism and lowering expectations
Uses avoidance or seeking reassurance from others to reduce the risk of being evaluated and maintain a sense of security
Weakening emotional fluctuations with rational narratives, avoiding facing shame and regret directly

object_relations.self_representation: An incompetent person, prone to failing and missing opportunities
object_relations.object_representation: Harsh judges or more superior others (especially those with degrees)

object_relations.self_representation: A caregiver who sacrifices for the family
object_relations.object_representation: Grandparents/family who need care and dependence

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When required to complete tasks needing critical thinking, or when needing to show ability in relationships
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Others (or the counselor) will scrutinize me critically like 'people with degrees', and once I fail will think I am stupid
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Speaks in a cautious, constricted tone, preemptively belittling herself or apologizing, taking on fewer tasks, trying to hand decision-making and evaluation authority back to the other party.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing the positive meaning of the decision to drop out, or receiving positive feedback from others
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Positive feedback not credible or 'not counting', worrying that once accepted, one must face the pain and regret of not finishing school
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Talks about experiences in an objective, fact-listing way, avoids emotion words and subjective feelings, tone flat, shortens the time spent on emotional topics.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the relationship becomes close and the other party both supports and challenges (such as requiring tasks to be completed more independently)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The other party may withdraw support or raise standards, ultimately exposing my incompetence
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizing external conditions or the reason 'I do not have a degree' to interpret avoidance or Withdrawal, using gentle but avoidant expressions to Displace the topic, reducing self-exposure.

manifestations: Strongly binds self-worth to educational credentials; after dropping out, finds it hard to continuously experience meaning from the choice of caring for family
Repeatedly indulging in counterfactual thinking of 'if I had not dropped out', ignoring current contributions and abilities
outcomes: Interpersonal tension (pushing others away or over-relying on others)

manifestations: Chose to drop out of school due to family responsibilities, long feeling torn and regretful between personal development and family obligations
'Logically knows it is the right thing to do', but emotionally finds it hard to accept the limitations the choice brings
Knowing supporters are around yet hard to open up about feelings of inferiority
In relationships, either distancing others or excessively seeking comfort
outcomes: Limited emotional connection and reduced sense of being understood
Dependence and avoidance alternate, further weakening self-efficacy

contact_model.definition: The individual has maladaptive self-Reflection and introspection, containing excessive self-limitation and self-harshness, being overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequently self-deprecates and apologizes in advance to avoid being evaluated
Overly cautious before speaking, repeatedly confirming whether it is 'correct enough'

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Treats the social standard 'education = ability/value' as the criterion for self-judgment
Language reflects 'if I had finished college, things would not be like this'

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Worries others will see me as 'very stupid', and accordingly avoids interaction or seeks reassurance
Presetting others' negative evaluations in situations requiring demonstrating ability

positive_force: Has a strong sense of responsibility and capacity for care (dropped out to care for grandparents)
Has supportive family and friends as potential resources
Excellent High school academic performance (valedictorian), suggesting Good Learning and competence potential
Willing to try reality testing and restructuring thoughts, able to identify thinking biases
Able to realize the counterexample 'degree holders may also not be good at finance', having the basis for gathering evidence
negative_force: Persistent Self-deprecation and overgeneralization, generalizing a single decision into overall incompetence
Mental filtering and negating the positive, treating current strengths and contributions as 'not counting'
High dependence on external recognition alternates with interpersonal avoidance / excessive reassurance-seeking
The rumination habit of 'if only I had...' leads to immersion in regret
Strong failure Anticipation when needing to demonstrate ability, lowering proactive attempts and self-efficacy

target_behavior.behavior: Self-deprecation and global negative labels ('I am stupid')
antecedent: Facing tasks requiring critical thinking or problem solving
Reminded of the dropout experience or compared with highly educated people
Scenarios of important decisions and tasks needing independent completion
target_behavior.core_reason: Internalizing the dropout experience as the core belief 'education = worth', and interpreting current ability through it; long-term self-criticism Reinforced the sense of incompetence and failure Anticipation
target_behavior.function: Avoiding possible failure and external negative evaluation, reducing Anxiety and shame in the short term; gaining security by lowering others' expectations
target_behavior.consequence: Avoiding challenges and procrastination, decreased task completion, Low mood and Impaired self-esteem, further weakening self-efficacy

target_behavior.behavior: Interpersonal avoidance or excessive reassurance-seeking (approach-withdrawal alternation in relationships)
antecedent: When needing to display ability or provide help in relationships (such as helping a friend with finances)
Self-rating 'poor performance' afterwards and feeling embarrassed or ashamed
target_behavior.core_reason: Fearing being judged or rejected, projecting inner Self-denial experience as others' negative views, struggling to self-soothe
target_behavior.function: Reducing the risk of being negated through avoidance, or gaining short-term stability through others' reassurance
target_behavior.consequence: Relationship tension or increased dependence, further validating the self-schema of 'I am not good enough', reducing opportunities for support and growth
